memory_update.text: POWL should be retained as a high-priority underfollowed grid-electrical-hardware candidate because it has direct medium-voltage switchgear/electrical distribution exposure and explicit fiscal 2026 backlog evidence tied to data centers, AI capacity growth, and electric utility demand.

MYRG should be retained as a second-order infrastructure-provider candidate for the same node; the key verification path is backlog mix by utility T&D, substation, data-center, and commercial/industrial electrical construction.
ETN remains the reference leader for market-pricing and demand validation, but should not dominate the underfollowed discovery lane because it is already a high-attention mega-cap.

Further Layer 1B searches should look for US-listed niche suppliers in transformer components, reclosers, relays, busway, cable accessories, substation automation, testing/inspection, and electrical distributors; likely candidates may be hidden under industrial-components or construction-services labels.

node: Large transformers, switchgear, breakers, busway, substations, and electrical balance-of-system
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-stock universe for the grid electrical hardware chokepoint. The strongest reference signal is Eaton, where Electrical Americas orders/backlog and data-center momentum define the category. The underfollowed lane is better represented by Powell Industries, a smaller custom-engineered electrical-energy control and distribution supplier with explicit medium-voltage switchgear, utility, and data-center backlog evidence, and MYR Group, a specialty electrical contractor tied to transmission, distribution, substations, and commercial/industrial data-center electrical buildout. These are research candidates only, not buy/sell recommendations.
